title: fix(metadata): the object read's sortability follows the caller's field permission for every caller class (#22250)
body:
Fixes #22250
Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What this does

For one caller, the object metadata read and the data route disagreed about a field that caller's field-level permission marks unreadable. The `sortability` projection served beside the schema on `GET /meta/object/NAME` marked that field `sortable: true` for a platform-admin or organization-admin caller, while the data route refuses a sort or filter on it with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`.

After this PR, the `sortability` projection is derived from the caller's own field permission for every caller class. The object definition itself (`item.fields`) is unchanged: whole for the exempt classes, because Studio and Setup authoring need it, and masked for everyone else. The data route and the permission read are unchanged.

## Measured first: the exemption and its stated reason

- **Where it is.** `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt` in `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts` (ADR-0106 D4). It exempts `isSystem` and any caller holding `manage_metadata`, `studio.access` or `setup.access`. The platform-admin set holds all three. An organization admin holds `setup.access`. `resolveObjectSchemaMaskPosture` answers such a caller `passthrough` / `exempt` before it asks the security service.
- **Its stated reason.** ADR-0106 D4: "Studio/Setup authoring requires the full schema." The code adds the write-gate derivation: a projected read sent back by a `PUT` would delete the fields it withheld. So this is the triage ruling's first branch: keep the definition read for authoring, and make the runtime projections agree with the caller's field permission.
- **Dispatch assumption M2 was partly wrong.** The sortability projection (`translateMetaEnvelope` in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, which both transports call) already read the post-mask document. For an exempt caller, though, that document is the unmasked one, so the projection inherited the exemption.
- **Picker-facing field lists on the server.** `sortability` is the only runtime projection the object read serves beside the definition. The list read and the layered view serve definitions only, with no projection. `item.fields` is itself the definition the ruling keeps for authoring. objectui handles its pickers against the permission read on its side (objectui#11925, objectui#11943).

## Door table: `examples/app-showcase`, real boot

Setup: `showcase_client_liaison` (which marks `showcase_project.budget`, `spent` and `budget_remaining` as `readable: false`) is bound to the `everyone` position. Callers: the seeded platform admin; `phone.demo` promoted to organization `admin`; `auditor.demo` as a member. Base is `c8bb3c8d9c`; head is `8b412a83e2`, the source change before the tests and the merge of `main`.

| Door | Platform admin, base → head | Organization admin, base → head | Member (control), base → head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /auth/me/permissions`, `budget` | `readable: false` → same | `readable: false` → same | `readable: false` → same |
| `GET /data/showcase_project` | field absent from rows → same | field absent → same | field absent → same |
| `GET /data/showcase_project?sort=budget` (and `?budget=100`) | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` → same | `403` → same | `403` → same |
| `GET /meta/object/showcase_project`, `item.fields.budget` | present (22 fields) → present (22) | present (22) → present (22) | absent (19) → absent (19) |
| same read, `sortability.fields.budget` | `{ sortable: true }` (23 entries) → **absent** (20 entries) | `{ sortable: true }` (23) → **absent** (20) | absent (20) → absent (20) |
| same read, `ETag` | `"39ce56dc"` → `"39ce56dc~3c4b8092"` | `"39ce56dc"` → `"39ce56dc~3c4b8092"` | `"39ce56dc~32c59ec2"` → same |
| `GET /meta/object/showcase_project/layers` (authoring) | `effective` 22 fields with `budget` → same | same → same | 19 without `budget` → same |

At head, all three classes are served byte-equal `sortability`. Conditional reads at head:
- The admin's own ETag answers `304`.
- The pre-change ETag `"39ce56dc"` answers `200`.
- The member sending the admin's ETag gets `200`.

After unbinding the set, the unrestricted admin's ETag is `"39ce56dc"` again (byte-identical, ADR-0106 D3), and `budget` is `{ sortable: true }`.

## How

- **`@objectstack/metadata-core` (`object-schema-fls.ts`).** The `exempt` posture of a caller exempt by capability, in a deployment with a `security` service, carries a lazy `runtime` question. That question asks the same `getMetadataReadableFields` the mask asks a non-exempt caller, at most once. It never rejects: a throw or an `undefined` answer settles `undetermined`, with one `warn`, so D4's "a sick security service cannot fault an exempt caller" holds. `resolveObjectSchemaRuntimeView(document, posture)` returns the view the runtime projections are derived from: the served document for every other caller, and for an exempt caller the `fields` their permission reads, plus a fingerprint of what it withholds. Each withheld name in that fingerprint carries a qualifier (`@` occurs in no machine name), so an exempt caller and a projected caller denied the same field never share a validator. `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt` now delegates its capability half to a private helper, which the resolver asks alone. That adds no second elevation read (`check:system-context-census`).
- **`@objectstack/rest`.**
  - `translateMetaEnvelope` takes an optional `runtimeDocument` (default: the served document) and derives `sortability` from it.
  - `createMetaItemAnswer` step 5 resolves the runtime view and passes it through the `translateEnvelope` port, which gains an optional third parameter.
  - In `rest-server.ts`, the cached arm of `GET /meta/:type/:name` treats a posture carrying `runtime` like a projecting posture: the protocol is not handed `If-None-Match`, the runtime view's fingerprint is folded into the ETag, and the `304` is judged against that folded value. The private `translateMetaEnvelope` and `metaItemAnswerSources` forward the view.
- **`@objectstack/runtime` (`domains/meta.ts`).** Only `answerMetaItem`'s `translateEnvelope` port, which forwards `runtimeDocument`. Every dispatcher item read already goes through `createMetaItemAnswer`.

## Tests

- **`packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.test.ts`** (new describe block):
  - per class (platform admin, organization admin, member): the runtime view holds only the readable fields, the exempt definition is served whole, and the member's view is the served document by reference;
  - one permission gives one view whatever the class; no validator is shared with the definition mask;
  - an unrestricted exempt caller is byte-identical; the question is lazy and asked at most once, and never for a document without `fields`;
  - `undefined` and a throw both settle undetermined with a `warn`; `isSystem` and a deployment with no service carry no question.

  One existing assertion went from `toEqual` to `toMatchObject` plus a `typeof runtime === 'function'` check, because the exempt posture now carries the function. Its "asks nothing" pin (`asked === 0`) is kept.
- **`packages/rest/src/meta-object-sortability-caller-fls.test.ts`** (new), per class, on the cached (default) and uncached branches:
  - the definition is unchanged, `sortability` never names the unreadable field, and it is equal across classes;
  - the member control still agrees with `resolveObjectSortability(item)`;
  - the cached arm's ETag is fingerprinted, the protocol is not handed the conditional, the admin's own ETag answers `304`, the member's ETag does not cross over, and an unrestricted admin keeps `"v1"` and its `304`;
  - a throwing service answers `200` with the definition and the unprojected `sortability`.
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-object-sortability-caller-fls.test.ts`** (new): the same per-class pins on the dispatcher's protocol-backed and registry-backed item reads.

**Reverse verification (from committed state, on-disk proof by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`):**
- **A.** `translateMetaEnvelope` was mutated to derive `sortability` from the served document (pre-fix behaviour). The REST suite went 5 failed / 8 passed. After `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest build`, `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in `dist`, and the runtime suite went 4 failed / 4 passed. Restore: blob equal to `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty; rebuild; preflight `--absent` with a clean tree; 13/13 and 8/8 green.
- **B.** The exempt posture was mutated to never carry `runtime`. The metadata-core file went 7 failed / 29 passed, all assertion failures. Restored, blob equal to `HEAD`.

The first B attempt used an undefined identifier and went red on a `ReferenceError`, so that reading is void. The second was refused by the tool because the replacement contained the anchor, so nothing was mutated.

## Local verification (head `3768ffad20`)

- **Package suites and typechecks.** All runs went through the shared verify lock. Exit codes were read from its `VERDICT` line.
  - `@objectstack/metadata-core`: 18 files, 425 passed; `typecheck` exit 0. Run on the `805f1ba09a` tree; nothing in this package changed after it.
  - `@objectstack/rest` at `3768ffad20`: 268 files, 5142 passed and 327 skipped; `typecheck` exit 0, with 0 files in `test-typecheck-debt.json`.
  - `@objectstack/runtime`: 340 files, 5508 passed and 19 skipped at `805f1ba09a`. At `3768ffad20` (a type-only test change) `typecheck` exits 0 and the new file is 8/8.
- **Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` at `3768ffad20` derives 64 commands; all 64 ran and exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 64 derived, 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (a derived zero: every entry records its exit code). An earlier pass at the merge head was red on `check-system-context-census` (a new `isSystem` read); `805f1ba09a` removes that read, and the census is green.
- **Lint, narrowed.** `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the 7 lintable files of the diff.
  - The population comes from `eslint.config.mjs`: `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']` minus `NEVER_LINTED`, and all 7 files are inside it.
  - The JSON reports 7 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules, as stated in the config itself), so this diff cannot change the verdict on a file it does not touch. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- **Real boot.** The door table above, on `examples/app-showcase` (`pnpm dev -- --fresh -p` on a random port, stopped afterwards).
- **Merge.** `main` was merged once, at `9865012548`, after #22265 touched `rest-server.ts` and `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` (a different region). `main` has moved since, with no overlap with this diff's files.

## Acceptance notes

These are observations only, read from source and not measured. No card is filed for them.
- **Partially masked fields.** For any caller, `sortability` keys on readability, while the security service's query guard also refuses a predicate or sort on a field served partially masked (`maskingRule`). Per `getQueryableFields`'s docblock, a masked field is readable but not queryable. No in-repo app declares a `maskingRule` today (showcase `permission-sets.ts`). Whoever touches `resolveObjectSortability` next should weigh it.
- **External objects.** On an ADR-0015 `external` object, an author-declared platform-injected column that the caller cannot read is re-added by `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` as `sortable: true` plus a caveat once the mask removes the declaration. This is the same for every class.
- **Spec description now narrower.** `ObjectSortabilitySchema.fields`'s description (and objectui's `column-sortability.ts` docblock) says the domain "is the served field map plus the always-provisioned `id`". For a D4-exempt caller whose permission withholds a field, the domain is now narrower than the served `item.fields`. Absence still means "no platform sort behind this name" for that caller, which is the consumer contract, but the producer sentence no longer holds for that class. That is a `packages/spec` text change, outside this dispatch; it is raised for the seat.
